claim: Between October 7, 2023 and March 30, 2026, 1,079 Palestinians — at least 235 of them children — were killed in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, per the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) casualty count. In April 2026, The Times of Israel confirmed that Israel's security cabinet had approved 34 new West Bank settlements in a single meeting — the largest number approved by any Israeli government at one time, bringing the total approved by the current government to 103. By comparison, six new settlements were formally approved in the 30 years between the 1993 Oslo Accords and the current government taking office in 2022.

sources.label: UNRWA Situation Report #217 on the humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip and the occupied West Bank (reporting period April 8–14, 2026), citing OCHA casualty data.

notes: Jacobs's markup numbers — '1,079 Palestinians, at least 235 of them children' and '34 settlements' — both check out exactly against OCHA (via UNRWA SR #217) and The Times of Israel. Whisper transcript artifact: '34 settlements at West Bank' = 'in the West Bank.' Her 'another violation of international law' is the long-standing UN/ICJ position on settlements (Security Council res. 2334; ICJ July 2024 advisory opinion) — attributed framing, not adjudicated here. ToI subhead carries the 103-total and largest-at-one-time findings; the six-in-30-years comparison is verbatim in the article body ('only six new settlements were formally approved by Israel in the 30 years between the signing of the Oslo Accords in 1993 and the establishment of the current government').
